gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a hot-weather daily energy figure or days on a power station. Dometic's own spec for the US CFX5 45 is 1.05 Ah/h at 32 °C (90 °F) outside and 4 °C (39 °F) inside. That works out to about 302 Wh a day, so a 1,024 Wh station (EcoFlow DELTA 3, Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2) lasts about 3.4 days in summer heat. OutdoorGearLab's 75 °F lab draw of 6.8 W gives about 6.3 days, so heat almost doubles the draw.
standout_why: OutdoorGearLab (cited) measured steady draw only in a 75 °F lab: CFX5 45 6.8 W, BougeRV 23 8.3 W, Everfrost 40 5.8 W, 320–400 Wh per weekend. It has no hot-weather figure and doesn't size a power station. GearJunkie (top result) gives battery hours for a few self-powered models (EverFrost 2: 36 h; BLUETTI: 4 days at about 70 °F) plus a general '40–70 W when running' line, but no Wh per day. I couldn't open gearandhome (cited; TLS error) or Car and Driver (fetch blocked). ChatGPT's own line ('500Wh … roughly 1–2 days') gives no source and no ambient temperature.
decides: It doesn't change which cooler to pick. It changes what to pair with it. For summer car camping, size the station at about 300 Wh per day for a 45 L compressor cooler, not the 160–200 Wh/day the 75 °F lab numbers suggest. A weekend in the heat needs about 600 Wh, which rules out 245–300 Wh stations (RIVER 3, Tenergy T320, ALLPOWERS R600) for anything past one night. The 1,024 Wh class is the right pairing for a 3-day trip. ChatGPT's '500 Wh ≈ 1–2 days' holds in heat (500/302 = 1.7 days) but undersells mild weather (500/163 = 3.1 days).
